newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Protests mount against Fujimori in Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: Protests mount against Fujimori in Bangladesh.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori arrived in Bangladesh on Saturday for a two-day visit to a welcome from his government hosts and noisy protests by left-wing groups.
Bangladesh President Shahabuddin Ahmed and Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina received Fujimori at Dhaka airport as military guards fired a traditional salute.
As Fujimori drove into the capital city in a ceremonial motorcade, left-wing students demonstrated outside Dhaka University against his visit.
"Go back Fujimori, you are not welcome here," chanted the students as riot police struggled to keep them from the streets.
Several political groups demonstrated on Friday against Fujimori's visit, which officials said would bolster ties between the two countries, and vowed more protests during his stay.

"We denounce the visit of Peru's hated President Fujimori who has dealt inhumanely with anti-fascist revolutionaries, including communist leader Abimael Guzman," said a leader of the Democratic Revolutionary Council during Friday's protest.
Guzman, leader of Peru's Maoist Shining Path rebels, was captured in 1992.
Dhaka protesters called Fujimori, the first South American head of state to visit Bangladesh, an "agent of U.S. imperialism" and criticised the Bangladesh government for inviting him.
In the afternoon, hundreds of activists of the Committee of Revolutionaries, another left-wing grouping, demonstrated in downtown Dhaka against Fujimori's visit.
The protesters, carrying placards and banners, called the Peruvian president a "fascist, killer and autocrat," witnesses said.
Police, however, foiled an attempt by the committee members to march to Dhaka Sheraton Hotel, where Fujimori is staying.
Government officials said Hasina and Fujimori would hold formal talks on Sunday aimed at boosting bilateral trade, which one official described as negligible.
The talks would be followed by the signing of two agreements on trade promotion and technical cooperation, the official said.

Fujimori on Saturday visited the Dhaka central office of the Bangladesh Rural Advancement Committee (BRAC), one of country's leading non-governmental organisations helping rural poor, especially women.
The BRAC offers small loans to rural borrowers to help launch income-generating activities.
Fujimori, who flew to Dhaka from Vietnam, will travel on to India on Sunday.
